# triangulation.library: PointPool

**Tier:** `geometry`. **File:** [triangulation.library](../triangulation.library.md). **Source:** [stdlib/geometry/triangulation.library.plato, line 590](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/triangulation.library.plato#L590).

Copied from source, comments included. A comment records intent. The body is the algorithm. Neither is a proof that the result is correct. Names resolve in the whole compilation.

This slice: PointPool, HoleStarts, Triangulate, NoFaces, NoPoints, PointPool, ComponentStart, ShiftedFaces, Triangulate, PlanarProjection, ToTriangleMesh.

```plato

    // The pool a region with holes is triangulated over: the boundary vertices,
    // then each hole's vertices in order.
    PointPool(r: PolygonWithHoles2D): Array<Point2D>
        => r.Holes.Reduce(r.Boundary.Points, (pool, h) => pool.Concatenate(h.Points));

    // Where each hole starts in that pool.
    HoleStarts(r: PolygonWithHoles2D): Array<Integer>
        => r.Holes.Count.MapRange(h => r.Boundary.Points.Count
            + h.Range.Reduce(0, (start, i) => start + r.Holes[i].Points.Count));

    // The region triangulated over the pool of its boundary and hole vertices, by
    // ear clipping after every hole has been bridged into the boundary.
    Triangulate(r: PolygonWithHoles2D): TriangleMesh2D
        => (r.PointPool, r.PointPool.TriangulateRings(r.HoleStarts));

    //==
    // # Multi-component regions
    //
    // A PolygonSet2D's components are declared mutually disjoint, so it triangulates
    // component-wise with no interaction between them. The only work is bookkeeping:
    // the components share one pool in the result, so each component's faces are
    // shifted by the vertices the earlier components contributed.

    // An empty face list. `MapRange` over zero never evaluates its body; the
    // expression exists only to fix the element type, which an empty literal cannot.
    NoFaces(_: TriangleFace): Array<TriangleFace>
        => 0.MapRange(i => TriangleFace(VertexIndex(i), VertexIndex(i), VertexIndex(i)));

    // An empty point list, for the same reason.
    NoPoints(_: Point2D): Array<Point2D>
        => 0.MapRange(i => Point2D(0.0, 0.0));

    // The pool a set is triangulated over: each component's own pool, in order.
    PointPool(s: PolygonSet2D): Array<Point2D>
        => s.Polygons.Reduce(Point2D.NoPoints, (pool, r) => pool.Concatenate(r.PointPool));

    // Where component `k`'s vertices start in that pool.
    ComponentStart(s: PolygonSet2D, k: Integer): Integer
        => k.Range.Reduce(0, (start, i) => start + s.Polygons[i].PointPool.Count);

    // The faces carried from a component's own pool into the set's shared one.
    ShiftedFaces(faces: Array<TriangleFace>, offset: Integer): Array<TriangleFace>
        => faces.Map(f => TriangleFace(
            VertexIndex(f.A.Value + offset),
            VertexIndex(f.B.Value + offset),
            VertexIndex(f.C.Value + offset)));

    // The set triangulated over the concatenated pools of its components. An empty
    // set yields an empty mesh, which is the honest answer rather than a
    // precondition — Boolean operations produce empty results routinely.
    Triangulate(s: PolygonSet2D): TriangleMesh2D
        => (s.PointPool, s.Polygons.Count.Range.Reduce(TriangleFace.NoFaces, (faces, k)
            => faces.Concatenate(s.Polygons[k].Triangulate.Faces.ShiftedFaces(s.ComponentStart(k)))));

    //==
    // # Planar polygons in space
    //
    // A Polygon3D is planar by declaration, so it triangulates by projecting into its
    // own plane, clipping there, and keeping the faces: the projection is
    // index-preserving, so the resulting faces index the ORIGINAL space points and no
    // lifting step is needed.

    // The polygon's vertices in its own plane, in ring order. The basis is the one
    // `polygons.library.plato` already uses for planar containment, and it is
    // right-handed about the polygon's normal — u x v = n — so a counter-clockwise
    // face in the plane is counter-clockwise about that normal in space, which is what
    // makes the faces below obey the winding convention.
    // Precondition: non-degenerate area, so the normal exists.
    PlanarProjection(p: Polygon3D): Array<Point2D>
    {
        var normal = p.Points.VectorArea.Normalize;
        var u = PlaneTangent(normal);
        var v = normal.Cross(u);
        var origin = p.Points.First;
        return p.Points.Map(q => PlaneCoordinates(origin, u, v, q));
    }

    // The IMesh3D obligation: the planar polygon as a triangle mesh over its own
    // vertices, wound to agree with its normal.
    ToTriangleMesh(p: Polygon3D): TriangleMesh3D
        => (p.Points, p.PlanarProjection.TriangulateRings(0.Range));
}
```
